question: Which new therapeutic targets for ulcerative colitis, not yet treated by any drug in UC, have the strongest evidence to be tested first?
what_you_read: An ulcerative colitis evidence atlas: the summary of its findings (front page) and the orchestrator's decision: four targets to test first from each list of targets with no therapy in UC. Each decision card shows the list, the gene's dossier from the atlas data and the orchestrator's rationale.
selection_rule: The orchestrator chose 4 genes from group A of each list of targets with no therapy in UC (first-in-class, well known with no drug, repurposing, genetics first): group A holds the genes that stay among the list's first ten under every way of scoring. No chosen gene has a drug tried or approved in UC or IBD. Each choice is explained by its direction, cell, drug route, safety and first experiment, and a reviewer gives a verdict on each, with PubMed citations for every fact it adds.

blocks.title: First-in-class shortlist
blocks.note: Genes that rise in UC as a change of the tissue, with few UC papers and no clinical drug for any disease.

blocks.title: Well known in UC, no drug yet
blocks.note: Established UC biology (more than 15 UC papers) that no drug reaches.

blocks.title: Repurposing: an inhibitor for another disease
blocks.note: An inhibitor exists in the clinic for another disease; never tried in UC, Crohn's disease or IBD.

blocks.title: Genetics first
blocks.note: Inherited UC risk variants: the gene, cell and direction predicted from DNA sequence (AlphaGenome), checked against the rest of the atlas.

items.text: SERPINB5 has the most complete case: epithelial cells make almost all of it in all four atlases, its rise is intrinsic (adjusted log2FC (adjusted_log2fc = 2.109)), and two mouse studies report that knockdown or ablation worsened colitis. Its weak points are that both studies date from 2026 and that its role in colitis-associated cancer is unsettled: UniProt describes it as a tumour suppressor, while a study of IBD tissue linked its aberrant expression with neoplastic transformation.

dossier.stability: in the top 10 in 6 of 6 scorings

tissue.detail: bulk: intrinsic, 56% kept; per cell: +4.7 log2 (TA 1 +3.7, Cycling TA +5.3, Immature Goblet +6.1)

safety.detail: vital organs ≤ 5 nTPM, not constrained, no Mendelian disease caused by loss of the gene

dossier.proposed_experiment: knock-down or CRISPR knockout in patient-derived colon organoids stimulated with TNF and IFN-γ (read-outs: barrier integrity, chemokine release, epithelial death), with a wound-healing or organoid regrowth assay, since the gene rises in regenerating crypt cells [epithelium, 86% of its RNA, mainly TA 1 and Cycling TA]; a blocking antibody can be tested directly.

key_papers.summary: REG1B is one of five genes in a logistic regression diagnostic model for UC built from biopsy transcriptomes.
Plasma REG1B was one of nine proteins in a model predicting incident Crohn's disease years before diagnosis.
REG1B was one of five machine-learning-derived diagnostic hub genes for Crohn's disease with kidney stone disease, with high expression in goblet cells.
REG1B was among the genes with highest predictive importance for relapse after anti-TNF withdrawal in a UC biopsy machine learning model.

items.text: Direction: inhibit; a validated target. REG1B is epithelial in all four atlases and its rise is intrinsic (adjusted log2FC (adjusted_log2fc = 1.4585)). Literature: it is supported as a biomarker (a hub gene of UC progression, a diagnostic-model gene and a predictor of relapse after anti-TNF withdrawal), with no functional study in either direction, and its baseline level does not separate responders in any drug arm. Drug route: secreted, a predicted antibody target. Safety: not loss-constrained, no recorded safety events, but UniProt links it with regeneration, so blocking it could slow repair. First experiment: a functional test first, silencing or adding the protein in organoids from inflamed UC mucosa, before any antibody.

key_papers.summary: An antibody blocking the TLR4/MD-2 complex reduced colitis-associated neoplasia in mice, supporting that TLR4/MD-2 signalling promotes disease.
An antibody against the TLR4/MD-2 complex lessened DSS colitis early but impaired mucosal healing during recovery, so the net effect is mixed.
A small-molecule TLR4 inhibitor predicted to bind the MD-2 pocket reduced inflammation in endotoxemia and necrotizing enterocolitis models, but MD-2 itself was not directly perturbed.
Baicalein, which binds MD-2 and blocks MD-2/TLR4 complex formation, alleviated TNBS colitis in mice, suggesting MD-2 inhibition is beneficial.

items.text: Direction: inhibit, with a caution. LY96 (MD-2) is associated with ustekinumab non-response while the UNIFI placebo arm is not significant (padj (arms.placebo (UNIFI).padj = 0.144)). Cell: neutrophils make much of its RNA, so its rise reports in part cell arrival. Drug route: an inhibitor reached phase 3 in sepsis and covid-19 and was never tried in UC. Literature: in mice, TLR4/MD-2 blockade inhibited colitis-associated neoplasia and an MD-2 binder alleviated TNBS colitis, but another anti-TLR4/MD-2 antibody interfered with mucosal healing during recovery. Genetics: plasma and gut-cell Mendelian randomisation are not significant. First experiment: the existing inhibitor on inflamed UC explants, read early and during recovery.

Direction: inhibit; the risk allele is predicted to raise FIGNL1 in colon NK cells, in a confidently fine-mapped UC signal. Against it: Mendelian randomisation gives no support, and biopsies show no change. It stays in the decision because the genetics list has only five candidates and its prediction is confident; it is a hypothesis about inherited risk, not about inflamed tissue. The reviewer is against it; it stays because the rule takes four genes from each list and the remaining genetics candidate, RORC, has data against its direction. First experiment: allele-specific expression and silencing in primary NK cells.

key_papers.summary: A north Indian UC GWAS found an HLA-independent SNP signal at the CFB locus among novel risk loci, with no direction stated.
The IBD-associated CFB SNP rs4151657 is also associated with IgA nephropathy and with higher serum CFB and C3a levels; the study is in IgAN, not UC.
A CFB coding variant (G252S) associated with perianal Crohn's disease is loss-of-function, impairing cleavage, complement activation and phagocytosis, implying CFB function is protective.
The CFB R32Q variant has a derived allele protective against age-related macular degeneration, flagged as a candidate protective variant; UC is not studied for CFB.

items.text: Direction: inhibit, against a contrary signal. CFB rises with a pooled log2FC of (log2fc = 2.24), significant in seven of eight cohorts, its protein rises too, and epithelial cells make it as an intrinsic change (adjusted log2FC (adjusted_log2fc = 0.8989)). Drug route: an inhibitor is approved for IgA glomerulonephritis and paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria and was never tried in UC. Against it: a CFB loss-of-function variant linked to perianal Crohn's disease implies its function protects, the treatment arms show no response signal, and loss of the gene causes complement factor B deficiency, so long-term inhibition may reproduce that disease. First experiment: the existing inhibitor on organoids and explants of inflamed UC mucosa, reading epithelial damage as well as inflammation.

The atlas recommends testing first sixteen targets that no drug treats in UC, four from each list of targets without therapy: first-in-class SDR16C5, CYP4X1, CPXM1 and CHRDL2; well known without a drug SERPINB5, CXCL1, CHI3L1 and REG1B; repurposing INHBA, CFB, LY96 and SELP; and genetics first TUFM, CEBPB, FIGNL1 and CFAP90. Each was chosen from the most robust genes of its list and is argued on its direction, its cell, its drug route, its safety and its first experiment.

items.text: Direction: inhibit; SDR16C5 rises in UC in seven of eight cohorts. Cell and tissue: epithelial cells make it (transit-amplifying, cycling and immature goblet cells), the lineage agrees in all three other atlases, and the rise is intrinsic, with a retained fraction of (retained_fraction = 0.66) after the composition adjustment, so it is a change of the lining itself. Drug route: Open Targets predicts it tractable. Safety: it is not loss-constrained and has no recorded safety events; it has never been tested in mouse colitis. First experiment: silencing in organoids from inflamed UC mucosa, as proposed on the card. What is missing: any functional or genetic evidence; its only UC paper names it in a list.

dossier.predicted_effect: blood neutrophil +0.327; colon monocyte +0.100; colon macrophage +0.093; colon dendritic cell +0.085

items.text: Direction: inhibit; the UC risk allele raises TUFM expression, and Mendelian randomisation agrees: higher expression in sigmoid colon raises UC risk (odds ratio per SD (odds_ratio_per_sd = 1.191)), colocalising with the IBD GWAS and replicating in FinnGen and Liu 2023, and so does expression in gut plasma B cells ((odds_ratio_per_sd = 1.356)). This is the strongest causal evidence in the pool. Cell and tissue: the predicted effect is largest in blood neutrophils, while single cells place it in plasma and epithelial cells, and in inflamed MSCCR biopsies it is slightly lower, not higher (log2FC (log2fc = -0.188)), with no change in non-inflamed mucosa, which does not support the inhibition hypothesis in tissue. Drug route and safety: TUFM is a ubiquitous mitochondrial gene, so a drug would need to act in one cell type. First experiment: allele-specific silencing in gut plasma cells or neutrophils. Caveat: one instrument. The reviewer is against testing it first for these reasons; it stays because it carries the only causal genetic support in the pool, and the first experiment tests that support in one cell type before any drug is considered.

For the repurposing targets an inhibitor already exists for another disease, but the data argue for caution: INHBA and SELP separate ustekinumab and placebo non-responders alike, so they mark severity, and for CFB a loss-of-function variant implies its function drives the disease. Genetics gives the strongest causal argument for TUFM, whose higher expression in colon raises UC risk (odds ratio per SD (odds_ratio_per_sd = 1.191)), although biopsies show no rise; the other genetics-first genes rest on sequence predictions. These are hypotheses from public data, to be tested in human cells first.

Direction: inhibit; the risk allele raises CEBPB, predicted in colon dendritic cells, and its mRNA rises in biopsies (meta-analysis log2FC (log2fc = 1.27)), with its regulon active in all cohorts. Cell: it is a broadly expressed transcription factor, made mostly by neutrophils and macrophages (neutrophil share (neutrophil_share_inflamed = 0.698)), and the predicted dendritic cell is not the main source. Against it: gut-cell Mendelian randomisation points the other way without reaching significance, and its baseline level separates ustekinumab and placebo non-responders alike. Drug route: a transcription factor is hard to drug, though nintedanib alleviated DSS colitis in mice by inhibiting CEBPB signalling. First experiment: silencing in monocyte-derived dendritic cells carrying the risk allele.

key_papers.summary: CHI3L1 is induced in inflamed mucosa including UC, and anti-CHI3L1 antibody reduced bacterial invasion and DSS colitis.
Chi3l1 knockout mice develop more severe colitis but less colitis-associated cancer, so it protects epithelium yet promotes tumor growth.
Mutating the chitin-binding motif of CHI3L1 in colonic epithelial cells reduces Akt activation and IL-8 and TNF-alpha secretion.
CHI3L1 enhances bacterial adhesion to colonic epithelial cells; blocking or silencing it reduces adhesion.

items.text: Direction: inhibit, with a caution. CHI3L1 has one of the largest increases (inflamed MSCCR log2FC (log2fc = 3.8187), up in all eight cohorts) and its protein rises too (log2 ratio (log2_ratio = 0.607)), which makes it a marker first. Cell and tissue: fibroblasts make it in Smillie 2019, but neutrophils make a large share in Gubatan 2026, and part of the rise survives adjustment (adjusted log2FC (adjusted_log2fc = 1.3967)). Function: an anti-CHI3L1 antibody reduced DSS colitis, but knockout mice develop more severe colitis, so blocking it could harm the epithelium. Drug route: secreted, predicted antibody and small-molecule target. Genetics: plasma and colon Mendelian randomisation are not significant. First experiment: a blocking antibody on inflamed UC fibroblasts and on epithelial organoids in parallel, to see benefit and harm in one test.

dossier.predicted_effect: colon goblet cell +0.041; blood regulatory T cell +0.039; blood neutrophil +0.039; colon enterocyte +0.034

items.text: Direction: inhibit; the risk allele is predicted to raise CFAP90 in colon goblet cells and several blood cell types, in a confidently fine-mapped UC signal. Against it: no Mendelian randomisation support and no change in biopsies. Like FIGNL1, it is a hypothesis about inherited risk; the first step is to confirm the predicted effect of the variant on expression in goblet cells before any functional test. The reviewer is against it for the same reasons as FIGNL1, and it stays for the same reason.

items.text: Direction: inhibit; SERPINB5 rises in all eight cohorts, by (log2fc = 2.0451) log2 units in inflamed against non-inflamed mucosa of the same patients. Cell and tissue: epithelial cells make almost all of it (share (dominant_lineage_share = 0.953)), in all four atlases, and the rise is intrinsic (adjusted log2FC (adjusted_log2fc = 2.109)). Function: two 2026 mouse studies report that knockdown or ablation protected against colitis, which is the strongest functional support in the pool, though both date from 2026. Drug route: Open Targets predicts an antibody and a small-molecule route. Safety: it is not loss-constrained. UniProt describes it as a tumour suppressor, but a study of IBD tissue linked its aberrant expression with disease activity and neoplastic transformation and proposed targeting it for control of disease activity and cancer prophylaxis, so its role in colitis-associated cancer is unsettled and long-term inhibition still needs care. First experiment: silencing in organoids from inflamed UC mucosa stimulated with TNF.

key_papers.summary: CPXM1 was among the proteins secreted at different levels by IFN-gamma-stimulated human intestinal endothelial cells, with its role in IBD described as little known.

items.text: Direction: inhibit; CPXM1 rises in UC with a pooled log2FC of (log2fc = 1.8968), significant in seven of eight cohorts, and is already raised in non-inflamed mucosa ((log2fc = 1.0059)), so it tracks the disease, not only local inflammation. Cell and tissue: fibroblasts make it (stromal in Smillie 2019, Garrido-Trigo 2023 and GSE282122, epithelial in Gubatan 2026), and part of the rise survives the composition adjustment (adjusted log2FC (adjusted_log2fc = 1.057)). Drug route: an antibody is the predicted modality. Safety: it is not loss-constrained and has no recorded safety events. First experiment: blocking or silencing it in primary fibroblasts from inflamed UC mucosa. What is missing: plasma Mendelian randomisation is not significant, it has never been tested in mouse colitis, and its literature is one expression paper.

The first-in-class choices are changes of the lining or the stroma that survive the composition adjustment, such as SDR16C5 (retained fraction (retained_fraction = 0.66)), but the literature reviews found no functional study of any of them, and several genes of that pool were set aside because their rise mostly reports cells arriving: LILRA1 and CEACAM4 are neutrophil transcripts and PCDH17 keeps only (retained_fraction = 0.098) of its rise.

key_papers.summary: Cxcl1 intestinal expression rises with DSS dose in mouse colitis, alongside other cytokines; the paper's focus is fecal lipocalin 2.
In mice with colitis or PSC, leaky gut raises hepatocyte CXCL1, recruiting MDSCs that promote cholangiocarcinoma.
Depleting intestinal macrophages and dendritic cells worsens DSS colitis and raises CXCL1 mRNA with neutrophil influx.
Nod1-deficient mice infected with C. difficile make less CXCL1 and recruit fewer neutrophils; CXCL1 itself was not perturbed.

items.text: Direction: inhibit; CXCL1 rises across cohorts with a pooled log2FC of (log2fc = 3.6892). Cell and tissue: in Gubatan 2026 single cells inflammatory fibroblasts send it to CXCR2 on neutrophils and to ACKR1 on endothelium, and UniProt records its chemotactic activity for neutrophils; most of its bulk rise is explained by cell proportions, so blocking it would act on neutrophil recruitment rather than on a change of the tissue. Drug route: secreted, a predicted antibody target, with no drug against CXCL1 itself. Safety: not loss-constrained, no recorded safety events. First experiment: a neutralising antibody in a co-culture of inflamed UC fibroblasts with blood neutrophils, reading neutrophil migration. Caveat: the circuit is co-expression, not proof of signalling, and plasma Mendelian randomisation is not significant.

key_papers.summary: Inhba (activin A) is a JunB target and recombinant activin A restored IL-17A and Rorc during pathogenic Th17 differentiation, suggesting it supports Th17 pathogenicity.
INHBA was overexpressed in baseline mucosal biopsies of UC patients who failed anti-TNF therapy and is part of a five-mRNA panel predicting non-response.
INHBA was among 13 candidate blood predictors of anti-TNF response in paediatric IBD but was not among the four validated significant genes.
Activin A (INHBA-encoded) and CCR2 drive macrophage-mediated testicular fibrosis in mouse orchitis, and the activin A antagonist follistatin reduced damage; not an intestinal model.

items.text: Direction: inhibit; INHBA (activin A) rises with a pooled log2FC of (log2fc = 2.6188). Cell and tissue: fibroblasts and macrophages make it and the lineage does not replicate across atlases; part of the rise survives adjustment (adjusted log2FC (adjusted_log2fc = 0.6949)). Drug route: an inhibitor is approved for ulcerative colitis and was never tried in UC or IBD. Literature: it was overexpressed in baseline biopsies of patients who failed anti-TNF therapy, but in this atlas it separates ustekinumab and placebo non-responders alike, so it marks severity. Safety: it is strongly loss-constrained (LOEUF (loeuf = 0.166)). In experimental colitis, administration of follistatin attenuated inflammatory cell infiltration, which supports blocking activin signalling. First experiment: the existing inhibitor on inflamed UC fibroblasts and macrophages, then on explants of inflamed mucosa.

dossier.stability: in the top 10 in 6 of 6 scorings

tissue.detail: bulk: partly composition, 25% kept; per cell: +1.7 log2 (Post-capillary Venules +1.8, Plasma +0.4, Endothelial +0.5)

cell.detail: stromal 86% of transcripts; same lineage in 3 of 3 other atlases (Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026, GSE282122); in situ Endothelial

druggable.detail: inhibitor approved (Crizanlizumab) for sickle cell anemia; never tried in UC, Crohn's disease or IBD

literature.detail: only 6 expression, 1 biomarker (outside IBD: pathogenic in mouse (PMID 37064877); outside IBD: pathogenic in cells (PMID 39665236))

dossier.proposed_experiment: Test Crizanlizumab (approved) in the cell system that makes the gene [endothelium, 84% of its RNA, mainly Post-capillary Venules and Endothelial]; read-outs: ICAM1 and VCAM1, leukocyte adhesion and transmigration, permeability. Then on explants of inflamed UC mucosa, and compare its dose with the one used in its approved or trial indication.

key_papers.summary: Activated platelets (CD62-P positive) falling after the first leukocytapheresis session may predict response in severe UC.
Platelet P-selectin expression was measured as an activation marker alongside platelet-leukocyte aggregates, which were higher in IBD blood and lowered by thiopurines.
Endothelial P-selectin immunoreactivity was about 3.7-fold higher in inflamed Crohn's and UC gut than in normal gut, with no difference between the two diseases.
Platelet CD62P expression was higher in active and inactive UC patients than in controls, alongside platelet-leukocyte complexes.

items.text: Direction: inhibit; SELP (P-selectin) rises in inflamed mucosa (inflamed MSCCR log2FC (log2fc = 1.8372) against (log2fc = 0.4546) in non-inflamed mucosa), so it is a local-inflammation signal. Cell: endothelium sends it to SELPLG on neutrophils, and UniProt describes it as the receptor that binds activated endothelium or platelets to leukocytes. Drug route: an inhibitor is approved for sickle cell anaemia and was never tried in UC. Against it: plasma Mendelian randomisation supports inhibition (p (p = 0.484)) and its baseline level separates ustekinumab and placebo non-responders alike, and in experimental colitis an anti-P-selectin antibody did not significantly improve colitis. The reviewer is against testing it first; it stays as the last repurposing choice because the only other gene of the pool, GUCY1A1, carries a vascular risk, and the negative animal result argues for a human test before any trial. First experiment: the existing antibody in a flow assay of neutrophils over inflamed UC endothelial cells.

dossier.stability: in the top 10 in 6 of 6 scorings

tissue.detail: bulk: intrinsic, 53% kept; per cell: +1.8 log2 (TA 1 +1.9, Cycling TA +1.7, Stem +1.5)

cell.detail: epithelial 89% of transcripts; same lineage in 3 of 3 other atlases (Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026, GSE282122); 94% of epithelial RNA in the crypt zone, rising there: possible repair programme

druggable.detail: no extracellular part; Open Targets: Druggable Family; pocket 0.78

safety.detail: vital organs ≤ 11 nTPM, not constrained, no Mendelian disease caused by loss of the gene

literature.detail: only named in lists or reviews (1 paper): nothing specific

dossier.proposed_experiment: knock-down or CRISPR knockout in patient-derived colon organoids stimulated with TNF and IFN-γ (read-outs: barrier integrity, chemokine release, epithelial death), with a wound-healing or organoid regrowth assay, since the gene rises in regenerating crypt cells [epithelium, 86% of its RNA, mainly TA 1 and Cycling TA]; small-molecule tool compounds may exist (Open Targets ligand or pocket evidence). Then a knockout or blockade in DSS or T-cell transfer colitis (never tested in mouse colitis).

items.text: Direction: inhibit; CYP4X1 rises in UC in all eight cohorts. Cell and tissue: epithelial cells make it, the lineage agrees in all three other atlases, and its rise is classed intrinsic after the composition adjustment, so it is a change of the lining. Drug route: Open Targets predicts both an antibody and a small-molecule route. Safety: it is not loss-constrained and has no recorded safety events; it has never been tested in mouse colitis. First experiment: silencing or inhibition in organoids from inflamed UC mucosa. What is missing: any functional or genetic evidence; its only UC paper names it in a list.
